slot.brief: Two parallel wires with given currents; find net field at a point midway or at a specified location

stem: Two long, straight parallel wires separated by $20\text{ cm}$ carry currents of $4\text{ A}$ and $6\text{ A}$ in opposite directions. The magnitude of the net magnetic field at a point midway between the wires is

verdicts.working: At the midpoint, r = 0.10 m from each wire. With opposite currents, both fields point the same way at the midpoint, so they add: B = (μ0/2π)(I1+I2)/r = 2×10⁻⁷ × 10 / 0.1 = 2×10⁻⁵ T = 20 μT.

working:
The distance of the midpoint from each wire is $r = \dfrac{20\text{ cm}}{2} = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}$.

Since the currents flow in opposite directions, by the right-hand thumb rule, the magnetic fields produced by both wires at the midpoint point in the same direction and add up:
$$B_{\text{net}} = B_1 + B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi r} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I_2}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi r}(I_1 + I_2)$$

Substitute the given values:
$$B_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-7}}{0.1} \times (4 + 6) = 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 10 = 2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T} = 20\ \mu\text{T}$$

Independent check: At the midpoint, r = 0.10 m from each wire. With opposite currents, both fields point the same way at the midpoint, so they add: B = (μ0/2π)(I1+I2)/r = 2×10⁻⁷ × 10 / 0.1 = 2×10⁻⁵ T = 20 μT.
